title: K-flat affine pullback chart comparison
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of affine schemes [def-pc-scheme], $A=\Gamma(Y,\mathcal O_Y)$, $B=\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$, and $\varphi=f^\sharp:A\to B$. Let $P$ be a K-flat complex of $A$-modules [def-pc-module-kflat-complex]. Then $Lf^*Q((Y\to\operatorname{Spec} A)^*\widetilde P)$ [def-pc-derived-pullback] is isomorphic to the exact derived restriction along $X\to\operatorname{Spec} B$ of $Q(\widetilde{B\otimes_A P})$ [def-pc-derived-category]. The localization on $\operatorname{Spec} B$ may have an independent universe. This computes pullback of a given model, without an existence assertion for a representative of an arbitrary object.

source.place: Tag 08DW(2) (perfect-lemma-pullback), affine computation using Tag 08DV and canonical chart transport

proof.text: Translate the abstract module kFlat hypothesis into acyclicity of tensor with every acyclic complex using HomotopyCategory.kFlat_quotient_obj_iff and kFlat_iff_preserves_acyclic. Apply isKFlat_tilde to the termwise associated sheaf K on Spec Γ(Y,⊤).

For an open immersion j, tensorPullback j and restrictFunctor j are left adjoints to the same pushforward, so Adjunction.leftAdjointUniq supplies a natural isomorphism. Pull back K along Y.toSpecΓ using isKFlat_pullback and transport through that natural isomorphism mapped to complexes. K-flatness is invariant under a complex isomorphism because total tensor maps that isomorphism to an isomorphism and acyclicity is invariant under isomorphism. Thus the chart-restricted complex C is K-flat.

Extract the chosen derivedPullback counit from exists_derivedPullback f. Its functor is tensorPullback f by the specified object and map equalities. The counit is invertible at C. Compose with quotientCompQhIso and mapHomotopyCategoryFactors to identify Lf*Q(C) with Q(f*C).

Naturality f;Y.toSpecΓ = X.toSpecΓ;Spec.map f.appTop, tensorPullback composition, and the restriction comparisons give RY followed by f* isomorphic to (Spec.map f.appTop)* followed by RX. Whisker by tilde and compose with exists_tensorPullback_tilde_iso f.appTop to obtain (tilde;RY);f* ≅ (extendScalars;tilde);RX. Map this natural isomorphism termwise to complexes and evaluate at P.

Apply Q to the complex isomorphism and compose with step 3. Finish with the inverse component of RX.mapDerivedCategoryFactors, explicitly using source localization universe wS and target universe w. No derived category on Spec Γ(Y,⊤) or comparison of localization universes is needed.
